refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These functions allow the state of Varlink connections (either of individual client side connections, or of all connections of a server object) to be serialized into an opaque data blob and an array of file descriptors, and subsequently deserialized again into new connection objects. The connections themselves, any buffered input and output, and any ongoing method calls are preserved, so that the peers do not notice. The listening sockets of a server object are not covered. This may be used by programs that reexecute themselves (i.e. invoke execve2 on their own binary) to keep their Varlink connections across the reexecution, or to hand connections over to a different process, for example a worker process.

sd_varlink_serialize() serializes the transport state of a client side Varlink connection object: the input that has been read from the connection but not processed yet, the output that has been generated but not written yet, the file descriptors passed along with either, which replies are still expected, and the connection file descriptors themselves. It returns an opaque, freshly allocated data blob in ret_data and ret_size, and an array of file descriptors in ret_fds and ret_n_fds. The file descriptors are duplicates owned by the caller, and need to be passed on along with the data blob to wherever the connection shall be deserialized, in the order they are returned in. The caller is responsible for freeing the data blob and the array, and for closing the file descriptors. Settings the program chooses itself, such as the userdata pointer, the callbacks, the event loop attachment, the description, the timeout, whether file descriptor passing is allowed, or whether input is security sensitive, are not serialized and need to be configured again by the program after deserialization. Peer credentials are not serialized either, unless they have been explicitly specified when the connection was established, since they can be acquired from the kernel again. The peer's PID file descriptor is passed on, however, if it has been acquired already (for example via sd_varlink_get_peer_pidfd()), since it cannot be acquired again once the peer has exited.

sd_varlink_deserialize() is the inverse of sd_varlink_serialize(), and allocates a new Varlink connection object from the data blob in data and size and the file descriptors in fds and n_fds. On success, it takes possession of all passed file descriptors: those it needs are duplicated, and all of them are closed and their array entries set to -EBADF. On failure the file descriptors are left untouched. This function may only be used for client side connections, server side connections need to be restored via sd_varlink_server_deserialize().

Server side connections cannot be serialized individually with sd_varlink_serialize(), since they can only be restored together with the server object they belong to. Use sd_varlink_server_serialize() (see below) to serialize them.

Serialization is refused while a method call or reply is being dispatched, i.e. it may not be invoked from a method or reply callback for the connection being serialized, or while a method call implemented as fiber is suspended. Connections that have been disconnected already cannot be serialized, and neither can connections to programs forked off via sd_varlink_connect_exec3.

A server side connection with a pending method call (i.e. one that has not been replied to yet, with the connection object referenced by the program in order to reply later) is only serialized if sd_varlink_set_serialize_pending() has been called on it with a true b parameter while the method call was dispatched. Otherwise, the connection is disconnected on serialization, since the program would not be able to reply to the method call after deserialization. The setting is reset whenever a method call is completed, and defaults to off. The program is expected to remember an identifier of the connection, as returned by sd_varlink_get_connection_id(), in its own serialization, so that it can claim the connection again after deserialization. Server side connections that are in the process of being upgraded to a different protocol are always disconnected on serialization.

sd_varlink_get_connection_id() returns an identifier string for the connection that remains stable across serialization. The string should be considered opaque. It is owned by the connection object and remains valid until the connection is closed, hence the caller needs to copy it if it shall be used beyond that. The identifier is derived from the underlying socket or pipe, and is unique among all such objects existing at the same time. It might be reused once the underlying object has been destroyed, though.

sd_varlink_server_serialize() serializes all connections of a Varlink server object, in the same way as sd_varlink_serialize() does for client side connections, including the method call currently pending on each connection. Connections with pending method calls that have not been marked with sd_varlink_set_serialize_pending() are disconnected first. The listening sockets of the server are not included in the serialization, and need to be passed on by the program itself.

sd_varlink_server_deserialize() restores the connections serialized with sd_varlink_server_serialize() into the specified server object. Before this function is called, the server object should be fully set up already, i.e. its flags set, its method callbacks bound, and the event loop attached. It does not have to be configured identically to the server object the connections were serialized from: the restored connections are configured according to the settings of the server object they are restored into, as for any new connection. For example, a newer version of a program may enable file descriptor passing on its server object, which then applies to the restored connections too, even if the older version did not allow it. Similarly, if SD_VARLINK_SERVER_INHERIT_USERDATA is set, the restored connections inherit the userdata pointer of the server object they are restored into (and not the one of the server object they were serialized from). Restored connections with buffered input are processed once the event loop runs. Ownership of the file descriptors is handled the same way as for sd_varlink_deserialize().

Restored connections with a pending method call are put in a table of unclaimed connections, keyed by their identifier. If two such connections share the same identifier (which is only possible for identifiers derived from inode numbers), the second one is disconnected right away. sd_varlink_server_claim_connection() looks up the connection with the specified identifier (as previously returned by sd_varlink_get_connection_id()) in this table, and removes it from there. The connection is returned in ret, without taking a reference to it, and the program should take a reference before replying, the same way it would while dispatching a method call. Once the program has deserialized all of its state, sd_varlink_server_disconnect_unclaimed_connections() should be called to disconnect all connections with pending method calls that no one claimed, so that their peers do not wait for a reply that never comes.

refsect1.title: Return Value
refsect1.para: On success, sd_varlink_server_disconnect_unclaimed_connections() returns the number of disconnected connections, and all other functions return a non-negative integer. On failure, they return a negative errno-style error code.

refsect2.title: Errors
refsect2.para: Returned errors may indicate the following problems:

listitem.para: An argument is invalid, or a field of the serialized data has an invalid value.
A mandatory field is missing from the serialized data, for example because data serialized with sd_varlink_serialize() is passed to sd_varlink_server_deserialize(), or vice versa.
The connection is currently dispatching a method call or a reply, and hence cannot be serialized.
The connection is to a program forked off via sd_varlink_connect_exec(), or is a server side connection passed to sd_varlink_serialize(), and hence cannot be serialized individually.
The serialized data is not valid.
No unclaimed connection with the specified identifier exists.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: sd_varlink_serialize(), sd_varlink_deserialize(), sd_varlink_get_connection_id(), sd_varlink_set_serialize_pending(), sd_varlink_server_serialize(), sd_varlink_server_deserialize(), sd_varlink_server_claim_connection(), and sd_varlink_server_disconnect_unclaimed_connections() were added in version 263.
